project.title: AquaSolar Living
project.subtitle: Smart PVT-Integrated Water Assurance and Domestic Hot-Water Cogeneration for Sustainable Villa Communities
project.team: Interdisciplinary undergraduate students, chemical engineering and mechanical engineering
supporting_themes: Water Quality, Health and Environmental Protection
Smart, Digital and AI-Enabled Water Systems

problem_statement.text: Centrally desalinated municipal water is available, but confidence in it may be lost between the utility supply and the drinking tap (building storage, pumps, internal plumbing), and households then use bottled water. The paper defines the problem as the absence of an integrated, low-energy, transparent final-point assurance system that maintains consumer confidence in already-desalinated water while limiting unnecessary additional treatment.
problem_statement.paper_explicitly_does_not_assume: That UAE municipal water is generally unsafe

background_claims.text: UAE water security depends extensively on centralized desalination.

Survey of UAE residents: majority rated tap water good or excellent, yet a larger share preferred bottled water; taste and contamination concerns (distribution systems, household tanks) were cited factors.
background_claims.caution: Reference year per reference list is 2015. Reported values are not simulation parameters.

background_claims.text: Sharjah study: most physicochemical parameters met national requirements, but several parameters changed significantly between mains supply and building storage; low residual chlorine occurred in a portion of locations, particularly storage tanks.
background_claims.caution: Single emirate. Reported values are not simulation parameters.

background_claims.text: 2026 systematic review: reported variations in physical, chemical and microbiological parameters in some household and tap-water samples; authors also note methodological limitations and potential sampling bias.
background_claims.paper_caveat: Findings must not be read as evidence that UAE tap water is generally unsafe.

background_claims.text: GCC research identifies consumer perception and organoleptic quality (taste, odor, mineral balance, chlorine perception, appearance) as barriers to acceptance of desalinated drinking water.
Household point-of-use treatment technologies are commercially mature. A review identifies real-time water-quality sensing and treatment verification as opportunities.

Commercial 'smart' systems often use elapsed time or cumulative flow as proxies for filter condition rather than measuring treatment performance; conventional systems often apply a fixed treatment train regardless of incoming quality.

background_claims.note: Reference 6 (RO household systems review) is in the reference list but is not cited at this point in the body.
background_claims.text: Depending on incoming water quality, unnecessary RO may generate reject water, raise pumping energy, remove desirable minerals, require remineralization, increase membrane replacement and cleaning, and duplicate central treatment.

A PVT collector generates electricity and removes heat from the PV surface via a circulating fluid; recovering heat can reduce PV operating temperature and supply low-to-moderate-temperature heat. Building-scale research supports combined electricity and domestic hot water use.
Dubai's Al Sa'fat green building system has mandatory sustainability requirements for new buildings; Abu Dhabi's Estidama promotes an integrated approach (no reference number attached for Estidama).
The project is not presented as automatically qualifying a villa for any green-building rating or credit.

system.description: PVT-powered residential water-assurance and domestic-hot-water cogeneration platform integrating rooftop generation, point-of-use drinking-water treatment and hot-water preheating.

existing_infrastructure.status: Paper states this hardware already exists

thermal_storage_tank.paper_role: Experimental thermal buffer, representative hot-water storage volume, basis for charge/discharge characterization and solar contribution; explicitly NOT the full daily hot-water demand of a household

existing_infrastructure.circulation_and_thermal_measurement: Stated as present; no component details given

drinking_and_cooking_water_target.scope_note: Only drinking and cooking water pass through the assurance unit; bathing, cleaning, irrigation and toilet water are excluded by design

dhw_design_basis_from_prior_research.scope_note: Refers to previous household-scale research (refs 12-14), not to this system's tank

energy_pathway.description: Solar radiation -> PVT collector -> (a) PV electricity -> pumps, UV, sensors, controller, data acquisition; (b) PVT thermal circuit -> thermal storage tank -> domestic-hot-water preheating

water_pathway.description: Municipal desalinated water -> villa storage/distribution -> inlet water-quality monitoring -> modular treatment -> final UV disinfection -> outlet quality verification -> dedicated drinking-water tap/storage

treatment_train_stages_in_order.note: Present in Pathway B; absent in Pathway A

treatment_train_stages_in_order.note: Used when incoming chemistry or product requirements justify it

water_pathway.downstream_storage: Paper mentions a 'dedicated drinking-water tap/storage' without describing it

minimum_necessary_treatment.definition: Apply only the treatment barriers required by measured incoming water conditions and the desired final drinking-water specification; select the lowest-intensity pathway able to provide the required final quality.

pathways.name: Basic assurance
pathways.stated_use_case: High-quality feed; taste/odor improvement and final disinfection assurance

pathways.name: Advanced dissolved-solute control
pathways.stated_use_case: Used only when source-water characteristics justify additional dissolved-solute removal

minimum_necessary_treatment.terminology_note: Week 3 text calls the same three configurations Mode A, B and C; they are identical to Pathways A, B and C

paper_limitations_stated: Conductivity, turbidity or other inexpensive sensors alone do not demonstrate microbiological safety.
Online monitoring provides operational assurance; periodic laboratory analysis provides verification.
monitoring.digital_platform: Translates measurements into a limited number of resident-facing indicators; keeps detail for engineers and maintenance staff; community-level monitoring may be centralized

planned_measurements.week5_draw_test: Representative household draw profile simulated by controlled withdrawals with cold-water make-up

implementation_plan.basis: Existing PVT system and tank, so no new solar-energy fabrication

weeks.outputs: Measured baseline of solar irradiance, electrical output, thermal output, tank behavior and parasitic loads; becomes the energy budget for the water-assurance design

weeks.focus: Residential water characterization and Water Assurance Pathway assembly
weeks.outputs: Commissioned modular treatment skid; baseline source and post-storage water characterization; if direct sampling is not possible the laboratory reproduces controlled storage-related quality variations
Decision matrix linking feed-water condition to lowest treatment intensity needed; controlled non-hazardous feed changes introduced
Simulated or measured solar electrical fraction and treatment energy per litre

weeks.focus: 150 L thermal storage and DHW validation
weeks.outputs: Simulated or measured thermal gain, tank charging and discharging, projected villa DHW contribution

weeks.focus: Integrated demonstration, community scale-up and techno-economic assessment
weeks.outputs: Simultaneous drinking water, renewable electricity, stored heat and monitoring data; reference villa package; 10-villa and 100-villa scale-up and a larger developer-scale community; economics, environmental impact, implementation model

success_criteria.rule: Successful only if ALL are demonstrated

items.text: Selected treatment configuration consistently produces water meeting the project-defined drinking-water quality targets for the tested parameters
items.dependency: Targets are not defined in the paper

items.text: At least one lower-intensity mode shows acceptable assurance without unnecessary RO under suitable feed conditions
Treatment electrical requirement is quantified and compared against measured production of the existing 6 m2 PVT array
Useful temperature rise and thermal energy storage are demonstrated in the existing 150 L tank
Water assurance and thermal production operate concurrently without compromising either subsystem
Key inlet, product-water and energy parameters are captured by a functional digital assurance platform
Measured data support a defined reference-villa package and a credible community deployment model

Solar integration strategies, thermal storage, techno-economic optimization and a solar thermal polygeneration plant in the UAE

prior_work.difference_stated: Earlier work produced new distilled water plus hot water from solar thermal energy; AquaSolar Living uses PVT electricity and recovered heat for final-point assurance of water already desalinated centrally

sanitization.removed: Promotional phrasing and self-assessment (for example statements that a feature is a 'major strength' or 'significantly reduces risk'). Retained only as tagged claims where they carry a testable proposition.
sanitization.retained_numbers_policy: Numbers from the paper are kept only as paper_stated_unconfirmed or reported_values, never as parameters.

known_defects_in_source.text: References 6, 10 and 11 appear in the reference list but not in the extracted body text.
Project-defined drinking-water quality targets (SC-i) are never defined.
Collector type, fluid, flow control and heat-exchanger arrangement are not stated, yet the paper claims a PV cooling benefit.
Carbon removes residual disinfectant and UV leaves none; downstream storage of treated water is mentioned but not analyzed.
The terms 'quality-assured' and 'solar electrical fraction' are used without definitions.
Week 1 is titled baseline modelling using TRNSYS but its body text describes measurement only.
No baseline comparator (bottled water, conventional full RO) is defined for the energy, reject or economic claims.
Microbiological safety cannot be shown by the proposed sensors, as the paper itself states.
Scale-up to 10 and 100 villas has no stated treatment of demand diversity or shared resources.

agent_directives.rule: This file is context only. No value in it may be copied into a parameter registry, code, test or result by the agent. Only the user may transcribe a value and set its status to confirmed.
Every field marked paper_stated_unconfirmed or reported_values is a candidate for the user to confirm, never a default.
Every item listed under unspecified_in_paper must be requested from the user. Do not infer, estimate or fill from general knowledge.
Do not treat claims_register items as established facts. Report their evidence_status and simulation_testable flags when they appear in any output.
References are unverified. Do not quote, extend or rely on their content without opening the source.
Out of scope for the simulation: consumer acceptance and behavior, taste, microbiological safety conclusions, green-building rating credit, regulatory compliance conclusions.
If this file and the user's later statements conflict, the user's statement wins; record the conflict in the assumptions register.
If a question cannot be answered from this file, the user's registry or the attached documents, answer UNKNOWN and ask.
